title: To Rei
coverAlt: To Rei title artwork: a letter and matching keychains beside a swimming pool.
summary: Fifteen years of letters. One summer left to remember.
intro: A short point-and-click story about memory, friendship, and words left unanswered. Explore a quiet hospital room and a sunlit swimming pool, examining letters, photographs, and objects to piece together a summer Haru cannot fully remember.
contributions: Built an object-led investigation across the hospital room and swimming pool.
Connected inspectable clues with an evidence collection interface so players can revisit what they find.
Shaped the transition from clicking through evidence to a final tactile interaction.

sections.title: A story told through what remains
sections.body: Letters, photographs, and familiar objects invite the player to reconstruct a relationship. The two environments offer different emotional perspectives on the same summer, allowing the story to unfold through observation.

sections.title: Teaching a different kind of interaction
sections.body: Most of the game is played by clicking. When a later interaction asks the player to drag objects together, a brief contextual hint introduces the change without interrupting the scene.

title: Sleepwalk
coverAlt: Two mirrored characters navigate a monochrome path of circles and crescents in Sleepwalk.
summary: Find a shared path through reflection, inversion, and shifting perspectives.
intro: A spatial puzzle project built around paired characters and changing geometry. Paths are made from simple graphic forms, but moving through them depends on understanding how the two sides of a space relate to one another.
contributions: Developed spatial puzzles around paired movement, supported surfaces, and reversible transformations.
Iterated on goals and interaction feedback through playtesting.
Worked on endings that transform the completed level geometry into a final composition.

sections.title: The surface is the interaction
sections.body: In the Rolling Girl level, both characters must stand on eligible paired surfaces before those surfaces can turn. The same shapes are both the route and the mechanism, making position part of every decision.

sections.title: Feedback without giving away the route
sections.body: An occupied turning face gently darkens. An unavailable action makes the occupied surfaces briefly shake. These responses communicate what the space allows while leaving the sequence for the player to discover.

sections.title: A level becomes an image
sections.body: The ending begins with the completed map. Its existing circles and crescents rotate and rearrange into a final illustration, connecting the puzzle's physical structure with its visual payoff.

title: Dear Little Alice
coverAlt: Dear Little Alice promotional cover with its ornate ivory and red title, bare black trees, glowing red flowers and light posts, a tiny maze doorway, and a small gray-and-red bottle.
summary: A small doorway. A changing sense of scale. An exit that asks you to look again.
intro: A surreal first-person exploration game that uses scale, navigation, and shifting environmental meaning. An uncanny forest leads toward a small doorway; shrinking changes what the player can access and how the surrounding space feels.
contributions: Developed the forest-to-maze exploration sequence and the change of scale at the doorway.
Iterated on environmental guidance, route access, and the readability of the drink interaction.
Connected the false exit, paper mechanism, and storybook reveal into a continuous ending.

sections.title: Scale changes access
sections.body: The player first encounters the maze doorway at normal size, then finds a bottle nearby. Shrinking happens in place, letting the same physical entrance become a route the player can pass through.

sections.title: Guidance that can be questioned
sections.body: The forest offers familiar visual cues alongside another route. After a loop, new cues appear while the earlier route remains visible, encouraging the player to reconsider what they have been following.

title: Line by Line
coverAlt: Line by Line title over the team's illustrated cover: a silhouetted detective, surrounding hands, theatre and evidence panels, and sweeping yellow brushstrokes.
summary: Designing readable spaces for a detective story solved through crosswords.
intro: Line by Line is a USC Advanced Games Project: a third-person detective game in which clues and conversations feed into crossword-based deductions. I contribute as a level designer, working on the theatre's spaces, navigation, clue placement, and camera framing.
contributions: Iterated on the balcony and control-room layout, including the relationship between adjoining spaces.
Adjusted prop and clue placement to improve visibility and click access.
Worked on camera framing and transitions across theatre areas.
Checked walkable routes and barriers while collaborating through Perforce.

sections.title: Making clues reachable and readable
sections.body: In a click-to-move investigation, a clue needs both a visible position and a usable approach. Layout work included repositioning a bag clue and checking how props, boundaries, and camera angles affect interaction.

sections.title: Connecting the theatre
sections.body: The balcony, control booth, and seating areas need to read as connected spaces. My work explored room boundaries, camera transitions, and the arrangement of existing props within the team's level structure.

title: Last Call
coverAlt: Last Call promotional cover featuring the four original role-card designs.
summary: Run the bar together. Balance the night's revenue with getting everyone home safely.
intro: A cooperative tabletop game about running a busy bar. Players take on the bartender, server, bouncer, and manager roles, coordinating actions while balancing revenue, customer intoxication, chaos, and safety. An online adaptation lets players try the game in their browser.
contributions: Co-designed the cooperative tabletop experience as part of the four-person design team.
Coordinated weekly tasks, responsibilities, and project deliverables as producer.
Organized task tracking and supported communication across design, art, and playtesting.
Helped bring the team's design process and takeaways into the final presentation.

sections.title: Profit has consequences
sections.body: Serving another drink can help the team earn money, but it also creates future demands on their limited actions. The intended tension comes from making customer safety part of the same decisions that keep the bar running.

sections.title: Coordination is part of the game
sections.body: Players plan actions with different role abilities and resolve them in sequence. An action can change the situation before a teammate gets to act, making communication and timing central to the experience.

sections.title: Keeping the team in sync
sections.body: A rule change affects the cards, rulebook, and next playtest. My production work focused on making responsibilities and updates visible so those pieces could move together.

title: Spatial Tinting
coverAlt: Spatial Tinting's pastel cube and color-matching interface.
summary: See through color. Read the structure. Find the rule.
intro: A spatial-logic puzzle that turns color perception into a deductive, perspective-driven game system. Players interpret how colored faces and structure relate, using observation as part of the puzzle-solving process.
contributions: Designed and programmed the project over seven weeks.
Developed the relationship between color perception, spatial structure, and puzzle logic.

title: Melodic Function
coverAlt: Melodic Function’s original itch.io title artwork, with a hand-drawn rabbit, moon, music, and quill.
summary: In this world, music obeys math.
intro: A rule-based music puzzle where mathematical functions become melodies players restore through interactive reasoning. The project brings musical patterns, mathematical curves, and a hand-drawn visual language into the same puzzle system.
contributions: Created the system and visual design over ten weeks.
Explored the relationship between mathematical functions and musical patterns.

title: Dismember
coverAlt: Dismember title art and its character against a city backdrop.
summary: A survival system where the body becomes a resource.
intro: A narrative survival system built around limb-based stats, durability, and gig-economy decision loops. Created by a four-person team over 72 hours.
contributions: Contributed gameplay programming and systems implementation within a four-person jam team.
Worked on the systems connecting body-part statistics, durability, and survival decisions.

title: Makeup Class
coverAlt: The physical Makeup Class game, with a makeup-palette board, cards, and game pieces.
summary: Beauty training becomes a system of pressure, comparison, and constrained choices.
intro: A turn-based board game that exposes how beauty training becomes a system of resource pressure, comparison, and constrained agency. The physical game connects its theme with the materials and routines of play.
contributions: Created the gameplay and visual design over twenty weeks.
Developed a physical game that connects resource choices with the pressures of beauty training.
